land.text: Bihar (subjugated 'in 1200') and Bengal, taken by Bakhtiyar as the Ghurid general in eastern India

predecessors.note: The Khalji page says the Khaljis 'first pledged allegiance to Muhammad of Ghor until his death in 1206, though their rule was mostly independent'; the ghurid-dynasty dossier records the loss in 1206. The Sena kingdom, whose Nadia fell in 1203-1204, is the sena-dynasty dossier's loss to the Ghurids. Repair of 2026-11-01 (review g-sa-a): the state now starts in 1206, not 1204; the infobox's 'Established: 1204 (Bakhtiyar's conquest)' falls while the land is Ghurid in the ghurid-dynasty ledger (sena-dynasty loses it to the Ghurids in 1204, ledger 9; ghurid-dynasty gains it in 1205, ledger 34), so a 1204 foundation would have collided with both.

land.text: Lakhnauti (Gaur), the Rarh and Varendra country of the old Sena kingdom (the mamluk-dynasty dossier's region for 1225-1227)

successors.note: 'In 1227, Iwaz was killed in battle by an army led by Iltutmish's son Nasiruddin Mahmud' (Khalji page); Bihar had passed in the 1210s. The Khaljis 'briefly regain control' in 1229-1230 under Balka and surrender in 1231 (infobox 'Disestablished 1231').

capitals.name: Lakhnauti (Gaur)
capitals.note: 'Capital: Lakhnauti, in northern Bengal.' Bakhtiyar's base for the Tibet expedition of 1206 was Devkot (Bakhtiyar page); his governor Ali Mardan had his headquarters at Barisal.

correction.text: Bihar and Bengal (West Bengal, Rajshahi and Rangpur)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1206-1214, now the first: after Muhammad of Ghor's death in 1206 the Khaljis hold Bihar and Bengal ('Bihar in 1200', Nabadwip 'three years later', Lakhnauti); the land is the ghurid-dynasty dossier's 1206 handover (ledger 38), 804 cells. Under Iwaz the territory 'expanded to its greatest extent' with invasions reaching 'Vanga, Tirhut and Utkala'; only Bihar and Bengal are drawn. The page gives no area. The earlier keyframe for 1204-1205 (a 60 km disc round Lakhnauti) was removed in the repair of 2026-11-01: it collided with sena-dynasty (loses the land in 1204) and ghurid-dynasty (gains it in 1205).

correction.text: Bengal without Bihar: Lakhnauti, Rarh and Varendra

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1215-1227: 'Iltutmish's forces captured Bihar in the 1210s', so Bengal remains. The Iltutmish page adds that Ghiyasuddin 'captured parts of present-day Bihar' later and 'extracted tribute from the smaller states of Jajnagar, Tirhut, Bang (in Bengal region), and Kamrup'; undated and not drawn.

region.text: Bihar and Bengal, Bakhtiyar Khalji's conquests (the ghurid-dynasty dossier's region for 1206)

ledger.note: 1206: the Khalji state of Lakhnauti stands as its own after Muhammad of Ghor's death. The Khaljis 'first pledged allegiance to Muhammad of Ghor until his death in 1206, though their rule was mostly independent' (Khalji page); the infobox gives 'Established: 1204 (Bakhtiyar's conquest)', the Bakhtiyar page has coins in his name (one dated 1204) and calls him 'a Ghurid military general', and Bakhtiyar's conquests ran 'After subjugating Bihar in 1200' and Nabadwip 'three years later'. Mirror of ghurid-dynasty ledger 38 ('was not Aibak's subordinate when he died in 1206'). The foundation was moved from 1204 to 1206 in the repair of 2026-11-01 (review g-sa-a) because the 1204 Lakhnauti disc was Sena land (sena-dynasty ledger 9, loss in 1204) and then Ghurid land (ghurid-dynasty ledger 34, gain in 1205); the 1204-1205 years are in this note only.

1210s: Bihar passes to Delhi. 'Iltutmish's forces captured Bihar in the 1210s, and invaded Bengal in 1225.' The decade is the page's; 1215 is the mamluk-dynasty dossier's year (its ledger 4), copied here.

region.text: Bengal under Ghiyasuddin Iwaz, as the mamluk-dynasty dossier draws it for 1225

ledger.note: 1225: Iltutmish invades Bengal and Ghiyasuddin Iwaz submits. 'Iltutmish's forces captured Bihar in the 1210s, and invaded Bengal in 1225'; Ghiyasuddin 'decided to avoid a conflict by paying him tribute and accepting his suzerainty' (page re-read 2026-11-01). Mirror of mamluk-dynasty ledger 9; the land is the Bengal core (Bihar had passed to Delhi in the 1210s). Added in the repair of 2026-11-01 (review g-sa-a, rule 4).

region.text: Lakhnauti (Gaur), the Rarh and Varendra country of the old Sena kingdom (the mamluk-dynasty dossier's region for 1225-1227)

ledger.note: 1227: Lakhnauti is taken. 'Nasiruddin captured his capital Lakhnauti, and defeated and executed him on his return to Bengal' while Ghiyasuddin Iwaz 'was away on a plundering campaign in Kamrup'; the Khalji page: 'In 1227, Iwaz was killed in battle by an army led by Iltutmish's son Nasiruddin Mahmud.' Mirror of mamluk-dynasty ledger 11-12. In 1225 Iwaz had 'chosen to pay tribute and accept Iltutmish's suzerainty'.

region.text: Lakhnauti (Gaur), the Rarh and Varendra country of the old Sena kingdom (the mamluk-dynasty dossier's region for 1225-1227)

ledger.note: 1227: the Khalji kingdom of Bengal ends. 'The coinage in the Bengal region was issued in the name of Iltutmish, and the khutba in Lakhnauti was also read in his name.' Balka's revolt of 1229-1230 ('Malik Balkha Khalji, an officer of Iltutmish, usurped the authority in Bengal'; Iltutmish 'defeated him in 1230') is a Delhi governor's rebellion, not drawn; the Khalji page's infobox dates the end to 1231.

1227: the tribute ends with the fall of Lakhnauti. The Iltutmish page says that 'in eastern India, Ghiyasuddin re-asserted his independence and occupied Bihar' without a year (between 1225 and 1227), so the vassalage may have ended earlier; 1227 is the year of mamluk-dynasty ledger 11 ('In 1227, Nasiruddin Mahmud captured Lakhnauti and executed Ghiyasuddin'), kept so the two dossiers agree.

wars.name: Bakhtiyar Khalji's conquest of Bihar and Bengal
wars.outcome: Bakhtiyar, a Ghurid general, 'subjugated much of Bihar in 1200' and took Nabadwip about 1203 and Lakhnauti by 1203-1204; Lakshmana Sena fled 'to east Bengal'. He died after the failed Tibet expedition of 1206.
wars.note: The land was Ghurid until 1206 (ghurid-dynasty and sena-dynasty ledgers), so no zone is drawn here.

wars.name: Khalji civil war
wars.outcome: Muhammad Shiran Khalji succeeded Bakhtiyar and imprisoned Ali Mardan, who escaped in 1208 and sought help from Aibak ('the first invasion of Bengal by the Delhi Sultanate'); Iwaz governed from 1208, yielded to Ali Mardan about 1210, and declared himself sovereign after Ali Mardan's assassination (1212).
wars.note: The Khalji page says 'Delhi took control of Bengal in 1208, then again in 1227'; the Bakhtiyar page has Iwaz governor in 1208. No land is recorded as changing state, so none is drawn.

wars.name: Iltutmish's conquest of Khalji Bengal
wars.outcome: 1225: Iltutmish invaded and Ghiyasuddin Iwaz paid tribute and accepted his suzerainty; 1227: Nasiruddin Mahmud took Lakhnauti and executed Iwaz. Bengal became a Delhi province until Balka's revolt (1229) was put down in 1230.
wars.note: The vassal interval 1225-1227 is the mamluk-dynasty ledger's (vassal_start / vassal_end); this dossier does not repeat it.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier; the extent is the ghurid-dynasty and mamluk-dynasty dossiers' admin-1 unions. Tribute to Iltutmish 1225-1227 is drawn as a vassalage, not as a change of frontier.

notes: No Cliopatria row (the Delhi Sultanate umbrella's Mamluk and Khalji shapes are other states; this slug is the Khalji maliks of Lakhnauti, 1204-1227, not khalji-dynasty of Delhi 1290-1320). START: moved from 1204 (infobox) to 1206 in the repair of 2026-11-01 (review g-sa-a): the Ghurid overlord keeps Bihar and Bengal until 1206 (ghurid-dynasty ledger 38), sena-dynasty loses Bengal to the Ghurids in 1204 (ledger 9) and ghurid-dynasty gains it in 1205 (ledger 34), so a 1204 foundation on the Lakhnauti disc collided with both; 1204-1205 are described in the ledger note only. The alternative (keep 1204 and have ghurid-dynasty ledger 34 exclude a 60 km disc round Lakhnauti, 88.14E 24.87N) needs an edit to a dossier outside this batch. TRIBUTE 1225-1227: now a vassal_start/vassal_end pair against mamluk-dynasty (its ledger 9 and 11); the Iltutmish page dates the re-assertion of independence nowhere, so the end is the Mamluk dossier's 1227. END: 1227 by the mamluk-dynasty dossier and the Iltutmish page; the Khalji page's infobox says 1231 (the revolt of Balka, 1229-1230, is a Delhi governor's, so it is not drawn; if a reviewer wants it, add Balka's Bengal 1229-1230 as a rebel entry). BIHAR: the Iltutmish page also has Ghiyasuddin 'captured parts of present-day Bihar while Iltutmish was on the north-western frontier' and 'occupied Bihar' again after 1227 (undated); 1215 is the mamluk-dynasty dossier's year for the first loss. TRIBUTARIES before 1225 (Jajnagar, Tirhut, Bang, Kamrup): undated, not drawn. RULERS: the Khalji page's table of rulers has garbled dates (Bakhtiyar 1204-1206; Ali Mardan c.1210-1212; Iwaz c.1212-1227; Balka c.1229-1230); no ruler strip. AREA: none on the page. Gazetteer names needed: Lakhnauti (Gaur) as a place.
